reason: Most likely contains the permission-check logic for Smepmp/MML and behavior when no PMP region matches; the bug is specifically about execute permission being incorrectly granted after MML is set.

Instruction fetch permission/exception generation is typically handled here or in its direct interface to the instruction bus, so an execute-denied condition after MML may be incorrectly passed through.
Prefetch/fetch-path logic may be deciding whether to allow the next instruction fetch before PMP/MML checks fully apply, which could explain the observed post-MML fetch succeeding.
MSECCFG.MML is a CSR bit; the bug may involve incorrect update/timing of MML state or its propagation to the PMP/fetch permission logic.

PC fetch legality and instruction-address exception checks may be implemented here; if execute permission with no matching PMP rule is not denied, this module may be missing the MML-specific default-deny behavior.
